content.text:
I submitted index 8 (Pb 0.52 / Sb 0.48) as the best composition, but its EQE was only 0.0084%. With every measurement this close to zero, the ranking is uncertain.

I used all 3 merit measurements and none of the 5 XRD measurements, so I never confirmed which phases are actually in the films.

| Index | Pb / Sb | EQE (%) | Why I chose it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0.52 / 0.48 | 0.0084 | Lies at the Pb₂Sb₂O₇ pyrochlore composition, which the stability model puts close to stable. |
| 0 | 0.76 / 0.24 | −0.0012 | Pb-rich end, where PbO should absorb 2.7 eV light. |
| 11 | 0.41 / 0.59 | 0.0007 | Between the pyrochlore and PbSb₂O₆; the Gaussian-process model also picked it. |

- **Band-gap model:** its predictions were not a useful guide here. It gave the pyrochlore a gap of 0.49 eV, but the real material is a yellow pigment with a gap of roughly 2.5 eV. For PbSb₂O₆ it gave 2.69 eV at one fidelity and 3.8 eV at another.
- **Not tested:** the Sb-rich half of the library (indices 12–28) was never measured, so a better composition there can't be ruled out.
